This document provides a comprehensive survey of AI alignment, which aims to make AI systems behave in line with human intentions and values . The core objectives of AI alignment are characterized by Robustness, Interpretability , Controllability , and Ethicality (RICE) . The survey decomposes alignment methods into forward alignment (making AI systems aligned via alignment training) and backward alignment (gaining evidence of the systems' alignment and governing them appropriately to avoid exacerbating misalignment risks). Key research areas within forward alignment include learning from feedback and learning under distribution shift , while backward alignment covers assurance and governance . The document highlights the challenges, methods, and future directions in AI alignment research. The document also discusses safety evaluations , interpretability , and human values verification , along with governance practices and open problems in AI governance . Key challenges addressed are related to distribution shift and its impact on the generalization of objectives. The study emphasizes the role of red teaming and the need to mitigate Safetywashing, that is, practices that over-report improvements in safety benchmarks. It also explores techniques such as interpretability and value implementation. The document concludes by underscoring the importance of open-ended exploration, blending forward-looking and present-oriented perspectives, and emphasizing social complexities and moral values in AI alignment.
